\section{Paper connection}\label{sec:perturbation-paper}

Throughout this section we use the paper's scoring vocabulary. ``rms'' is the root-mean-square error, quoted in units of the local mean spacing of the zeros. ``corr'' is the Pearson correlation (Chapter~\ref{ch:probability}) between two lists of numbers, for example predicted and true shifts: a number between $-1$ and $+1$ that measures whether the two lists rise and fall together. The ``null'' is the prediction with no fitted correction. ``In-sample'' means evaluated on the levels used in the fit; ``out-of-sample'' or ``held-out'' means evaluated on levels that were not used. An ``unregularized'' fit is one without the extra penalty on large coefficients (ridge regularization) introduced in Chapter~\ref{ch:least-squares}.
